title: Hamiltonian Simulation
summary: Approximate the evolution under a sum of terms with Trotter steps.
objectives: Say why a sum of Hamiltonian terms cannot just be applied one term after another, and when it can
Build a Trotter step for the transverse-field Ising model and repeat it
Choose the number of steps for a target fidelity, and predict how the error changes when it doubles
mission: Simulate two qubits under H = J Z⊗Z + h (X⊗I + I⊗X) with J = 1, h = 0.8 and time t = 2, starting in |00⟩, to see how many Trotter steps the non-commuting terms cost. Build qc with n_steps repeated steps, each e^{-iJ Z⊗Z dt} followed by e^{-ih X dt} on each qubit, using only rzz and rx. Choose n_steps so that the final state has fidelity at least 0.99 with the exact state e^{-iHt}|00⟩. The circuit may have at most 90 gates.

prediction.question: With a first-order Trotter formula and n = 5 steps the infidelity 1 − F is about 0.022. What is it about for n = 10?
options: About 0.022, since the error per step stays the same
prediction.explanation: The error of the state falls like 1/n, so doubling n halves it, and the infidelity is quadratic in that error, so it falls by a factor of 4. The exact values are 0.0220 for n = 5 and 0.0049 for n = 10. The error per step does shrink, as Δt².

hints: Each term of one step is a rotation. rzz(θ) is e^{-iθ ZZ/2}, so which θ gives e^{-iJ ZZ dt}? The same question for rx.
The three gates of one step go inside a loop over n_steps. dt = t / n_steps is already defined.
Start with a few steps and raise n_steps while watching the fidelity. Each step costs three gates, so 90 gates allow at most 30 steps.

challenge.mission: Reach fidelity at least 0.995 with the exact state e^{-iHt}|00⟩, for the same H, t and initial state as the mission, using at most 20 gates (only rzz and rx). The first-order formula needs about 10 steps and 30 gates for this, so use the second-order (symmetric) step: half a step of the field, a full Z⊗Z step, half a step of the field. Half steps on the same qubit that meet between two steps can be merged into one rx.
hints: The symmetric step is e^{-ihXdt/2} e^{-iJZZdt} e^{-ihXdt/2}. Look at what sits between the end of one step and the start of the next.
Two half rotations on the same qubit, one after the other, make one rotation with the angles added.
Five steps need 2 half rx at the start, 5 rzz, 4 full rx on each qubit at the joins and 2 half rx at the end: 17 gates, within the limit.
